tools.name: triage_log
tools.title: Triage a paste of log lines
tools.description: Paste log lines — combined, JSON, `uniq -c`, `<ip> <ua>` or bare user-agents, auto-detected — for per-line crawler, operator, purpose and cost of blocking, a rollup by operator and category, and every line whose address contradicts its claim. Log text, never a URL. Example: log='66.249.66.1 Googlebot/2.1' returns Googlebot, Google, search, verified.

log.description: The log text, up to 5000 lines. Mixed formats are fine.

tools.name: find_impersonators
tools.title: Find the lines that are lying
tools.description: Only the lines claiming a crawler whose operator publishes address ranges, from an address in none of them — 1887 IPv4 and 1056 IPv6 prefixes, 12 sources. Reverse-DNS operators come back with the command to run: this server makes no outbound request. Example: log='203.0.113.9 Googlebot/2.1' returns one impersonation.

log.description: The log text. Lines need an address to be checkable.

tools.name: summarize_by_operator
tools.title: Roll a log up by operator and category
tools.description: Aggregate only: who crawled you, how many requests each, what share, which category, and what blocking each would cost. Eats a `uniq -c` table straight from a shell pipeline. Example: log='412 GPTBot/1.2' returns OpenAI, 412 requests, 100%, ai-training.

log.description: Log text, or a `uniq -c` user-agent table.

tools.name: robots_from_log
tools.title: robots.txt from a log
tools.description: A robots.txt naming only the crawlers in your log, each with its request count and cost of blocking, plus a warning for any that do not documentably obey it — there the file is a request, not enforcement. Example: log='412 GPTBot/1.2', stance='block-ai-training' blocks GPTBot only.

tools.name: waf_ruleset_from_log
tools.title: WAF ruleset from a log
tools.description: nginx, Caddy, Cloudflare, HAProxy or Apache rules for only the crawlers in your log. The reply warns that a UA rule stops only an honest client, and that impersonation is an address problem needing the published prefixes as an allowlist. Example: log='412 GPTBot/1.2', target='nginx', scope='ai-training'.

scope.description: A category (default ai-training), 'all-seen', 'impersonators', or a stance.

io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo.name: crawler-log-triage
io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo.title: Crawler Log Triage
io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo.description: Paste access-log lines or a user-agent frequency table; get every crawler identified and attributed to its operator, an aggregate by operator and category, the lines whose claim their address contradicts, and a ready-to-paste robots.txt or WAF ruleset for what was actually in the file.
